input.quote: 11.5 Special, Indirect, and Other Losses. EXCEPT (A) FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS UNDER [ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8], (C) AS PROVIDED UNDER [***] AND (D) TO THE EXTENT ANY SUCH DAMAGES ARE REQUIRED TO BE PAID TO A THIRD PARTY AS PART OF A CLAIM FOR WHICH A PARTY PROVIDES INDEMNIFICATION UNDER THIS ARTICLE 11, NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
input.rationale: Section 11.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision in the Agreement. It is mutual and contains an acceptable set of carve-outs (fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, confidentiality/Article 9 and Section 5.8, and third-party indemnified damages), but it goes no further than excluding indirect and consequential damages. Searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed" and all "liable/liability" hits confirm there is no monetary cap on either party's direct liability anywhere in the document (Article 13 contains only force majeure; Article 11 otherwise deals with indemnity procedure and insurance). The rule requires a mutual cap at a meaningful amount; the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs) is also unmet because no cap of any kind exists, so this fails on a material term. The redline adds a single mutual cap sentence to the existing Section 11.5 at the greater of 12 months' payments by AbbVie and USD 1,000,000, keeps the indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs outside the cap (mirroring the exceptions already agreed in 11.5), and confirms AbbVie's Article 6 payment obligations are not capped "damages".

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs to Section 11.5
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article 11 waives consequential damages but leaves both parties' direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' payments and USD 1,000,000, consistent with our position that liability be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount. Indemnification obligations, confidentiality (Article 9/Section 5.8), gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and AbbVie's payment obligations under Article 6 are not treated as capped damages.

ops.oldText: EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.
ops.newText: EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BY ABBVIE TO HARPOON UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (USD 1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS UNDER [ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8], ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER THIS ARTICLE 11, ITS FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. AMOUNTS PAYABLE BY ABBVIE UNDER ARTICLE 6 SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO SUCH CAP.
